note: Shared by the server's and the client's tests (add-check A1). Every 'node' goes through `checkAddNode(node, { avatar })`, which returns null or { code, message }. 'reason' is the shared code. 'avatar' selects A5's budget and extras rule. The 20,000-primitive avatar (CR-M2) is not a literal vector: it is exercised by the server test file, which bounds the reply at 500 ms. Round 2 (REVISION-add-check-round-2.md) adds the R1 (__proto__), R3 (fail closed) and small S3 boundary vectors; the large boundaries (1,024 avatar vertices, 6,144 indices, 65,535 vertices) are generated in packages/server/test/add-node-boundaries.test.js, which runs both copies. richer-add (PREBRIEF-richer-add.md R1–R3) flips two world vectors to accepted (TEXCOORD_0, alphaMode BLEND) and adds the 'R1:' vectors; values JSON can't hold (Infinity, NaN in extras) and the 16 KiB edges are in add-node-boundaries.test.js. subtree-add (T1, T12): the tree vectors (the 1,024- and 1,025-primitive trees are generated in add-node-boundaries.test.js), labelled 'subtree-add: …': the bounds (256 members, 8 generations, 1,024 primitives), the D3 name form and names and ids unique within a tree, avatar-children, and material refs in message order (depth-first pre-order; the cross-branch pair tells it from breadth-first).
